policy.source: Google Books English One Million, version 20090715
policy.selection: Fixed source sample, filters and blend shares before scoring. Development only. Descriptive pilot, no automatic promotion or test selection.
policy.normalization: lowercase ASCII English words, internal apostrophes only; curly apostrophe converted to ASCII; reject punctuation tokens, digits, tags and non-ASCII words
policy.primary_metric: top-five accuracy after two graphemes, separately per suite
policy.limitations: All ten unigram shards, four of 100 bigram shards, four of 200 trigram shards. Shards are not assumed to be random samples. Counts are not upsampled to pretend full coverage. Source is older book language, not conversation. Version 1 may cross sentence boundaries. Pruning and sparse contextual coverage limit any conclusions about the full Google Books corpus.

selection_proxy.definition: Optimistic offline rank-sensitive proxy: each typed grapheme costs one selection; accept costs rank+1 among five slots; choose cheapest completion after >=2 graphemes, or type word fully. Excludes spaces, scan navigation/timing, errors and cognitive effort; not measured AAC switch savings.

algorithm: Unchanged 0.1/0.3/0.6 interpolated counts, personal learning disabled.
limitations: All ten unigram shards, four of 100 bigram shards, four of 200 trigram shards. Shards are not assumed to be random samples. Counts are not upsampled to pretend full coverage. Source is older book language, not conversation. Version 1 may cross sentence boundaries. Pruning and sparse contextual coverage limit any conclusions about the full Google Books corpus. Aggregated Google counts cannot establish or remove full-sentence overlap with evaluations. These are known regression suites. Exact integer mixture scaling is for offline probability comparison; it changes absolute count units and must not ship with existing personal-learning weights without a separate calibration experiment.
